claim: Excluding determiners is given as a defining property of pronouns.
evidence_summary: The real me retains person deixis and takes third-person agreement. CGEL treats a he or a she as common-noun uses.
finding: Seek independent evidence for conversion before deciding whether determiner-taking defeats pronoun status.
inference: Does determiner-taking independently establish that a person-deictic form has changed category?

evidence.passage: §10.2, p. 429. Excluding determiners is given as a defining property of pronouns.
evidence.example: The real me has a determiner and can retain speaker reference, yet takes third-person agreement. CGEL also allows a he or a she with a common-noun interpretation.
evidence.establishes: Deixis and agreement pull in different directions. To argue for conversion, identify evidence beyond the diagnostic whose necessity is being tested.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
